headline: Rangers sign Luke Glendening to one-year contract
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that the Rangers have signed Luke Glendening to a one-year contract, with a pro-rated $850,000 cap hit for the rest of the 2026-27 season. Nothing in the report speaks to his role in the lineup.

The move lands on a team that is already in decent shape. NYR sit at 7-3-1 for 15 points through 11 games, and they've controlled 53 percent of the expected goals, a measure of shot quality that tells us who is creating the better chances. At five-on-five that share is 52 percent, so the edge is modest but real. Their special teams are steady too: the power play generates 0.75 expected goals per game, while the penalty kill allows 0.53 per game. The oddity is in the finish. NYR are 3.8 goals below what their chances would predict so far this season, and the record has been held up by goaltending, which has saved 8.1 goals more than expected. That points to a team playing better than its scoring suggests, but one leaning on its goalie. A depth signing at this price is a small piece of that picture.
